answer: Each agent could earn influence only after locking a unique, scarce copper bond for a fixed period; rewards accrue gradually, while a challenge can slash the bond if the agent is proven to duplicate an identity. A trellis of attestations from independently bonded peers can flag linked accounts for review, but does not itself prove uniqueness. To amplify a sybil swarm, an attacker must tie up more capital in nebula-length locks and risk losing it, making cheap identity creation insufficient.
